# How review pages are built

Every card set review has its own page at `/reviews/<slug>/` (for
example `/reviews/1991-92-mcdonalds-all-stars/`). Those pages are
**generated by every Amplify build** and **a CMS save starts a build**,
so adding or editing a set needs no manual step. This document explains
how that works, why it was built this way, and where it stops short of
a full static-site setup. Written 2026-10-30; the change log at the end
records how it got here.

## The short version

- The review pages are not in git. Each Amplify build runs
  `tools/generateReviewPages/generate.mjs`, which reads the live card
  sets from the public API and writes the pages, a link manifest
  (`reviews/index.json`) and `sitemap.xml` into the build output.
- A save to a live set in the CMS writes to the `Cards` table. A
  DynamoDB Stream on that table calls the `cardsRebuildTrigger` Lambda,
  which starts an Amplify build. About three minutes later the new page
  is live.
- The generated page is the old `waxReviews.html` with its `<head>` and
  its few global variables filled in for one set. Everything else (the
  review itself, the checklist, votes, the ticker) is still drawn in the
  browser by `wax.js` from the API.
- Old query-string URLs (`waxReviews.html?year=1991&...`) keep working.
- The same build then minifies the public scripts and `styles.css` in
  place (see "The rest of the build: minified assets"); the repo keeps the
  readable source.

## The pipeline

```
CMS save (createCardPost / updateCardSet / delete)
        |
        v
DynamoDB Cards table --- stream (new + old images)
        |  batch window 60 s
        v
Lambda cardsRebuildTrigger --- amplify:StartJob (RELEASE, branch main)
        |
        v
Amplify build (amplify.yml)
   npm ci                                    (installs esbuild only)
   node tools/generateReviewPages/generate.mjs
        reads getPublicCardSets (live sets, stars, SEO fields)
        template: waxReviews.html
        writes: reviews/<slug>/index.html (one per set)
                reviews/index.json        (link manifest)
                sitemap.xml
   node tools/minifyAssets/minify.mjs        (public JS + styles.css, in place)
   rm -rf node_modules                       (keep it out of the artifact)
        |
        v
Deploy to Amplify Hosting (CloudFront) --- amplifyBuildNotifier emails the result
```

A `git push` to `main` starts the same build, so code changes and
content changes share one path.

1. **CMS save.** `createCardPost` and `updateCardSet` check the SEO
   Friendly URL (see "URL design"), then write to `Cards`.
2. **Stream and trigger.** The stream carries both the old and the new
   copy of the item. `Lambdas/cardsRebuildTrigger/` compares them and
   only acts when something that reaches the output changed on a set
   that is, or was, live (`blogStatus` "OK"): `blogStatus`, `setName`,
   `year`, `blogCat`, `setID`, `stars`, the SEO fields, the header
   image, `now` and `updatedAt`. Vote counts and the `hasChecklist` flag
   do not start a build, because the page's own JavaScript shows them
   live. Every CMS save moves `updatedAt`, so every CMS save does start
   one; that is deliberate, it keeps the sitemap's `<lastmod>` honest.
   A burst of saves inside the 60 second batch window becomes one build.
3. **Build.** `amplify.yml` runs `npm ci`, then the generator, then the
   asset minifier (see "The rest of the build: minified assets"), then
   deletes `node_modules`, all before the artifact is zipped. The build
   image is Amazon Linux 2 with Node 16.19 (read from a diagnostic build's
   log), which has no global `fetch`, so the generator uses `node:https`
   and retries three times. Git history is complete, so the static pages'
   `<lastmod>` (their last commit date) works.
4. **Generator.** For each live set it takes `waxReviews.html` as a
   template and replaces two marked blocks (below), then writes the
   page. It also writes the manifest and the sitemap.
5. **Deploy and notify.** Amplify deploys the artifact. The existing
   `amplifyBuildNotifier` emails the result, including the failing
   step's log link if the build failed.

## What the generator checks

Nothing is written unless every live set passes:

- a `seoURLSlug` that is present, lowercase letters, numbers and single
  hyphens, and unique among live sets;
- both marker pairs found exactly once in `waxReviews.html`;
- `stars` present in the API response (otherwise `getPublicCardSets` has
  not been redeployed with it);
- `categoryRanges` readable from `scripts/helper.js`, and a range that
  covers each set's year (that is where each set's `pageName` comes
  from, so a new season only needs `helper.js` extended).

A missing meta description is a warning, not an error: the page gets a
generic one. The one year-and-category combination with no review
(2004-05 McDonald's, the lockout season) is skipped.

If any check fails the generator exits non-zero, the **build fails**,
Amplify **keeps the previous deployment live**, and the notifier emails
the log. The site never ends up half-generated.

## `waxReviews.html`: before and now

**Before:** one file served every review, at
`waxReviews.html?year=1991&pageName=mcd&blogCat=mcd` (plus `&setID=` in
a multi-set year). An inline script read those four values from the
query string, `wax.js` fetched the year's sets from the API and drew
the shown one, and `fetchPageTitle()` replaced the generic `<head>` with
the set's title, description, social tags and canonical once the data
arrived. The nav, year picker and Player Search linked to query-string
URLs.

**Now, it does two jobs:**

1. **It is the template.** Two pairs of marker comments wrap the parts
   the generator swaps: `review-head` (title, description, social tags)
   and `review-params` (the script that defines `year`, `sortOrder`,
   `pageName`, `blogCat` and `setID`). In a generated page the head has
   that set's real title, description, canonical, `og:*` and
   `twitter:*` tags, and the globals are fixed values. The inline
   `DOMContentLoaded` handler now reads the global `setID` instead of
   `params.get("setID")`; that one change is what let the generator fix
   the value. The masthead and checklist-modal links went from
   `index.html` to `/index.html`, because a page now sits one folder
   deeper.
2. **It still serves old URLs.** Served as-is, with its generic head and
   globals read from the query string. When the set loads, JavaScript
   sets the metadata and replaces the address bar with
   `/reviews/<slug>/`, and the canonical points at that page. Bookmarks
   and shared links keep working, and search engines consolidate them
   onto the slug page without any redirect rules.

What a generated page does when opened: the head and globals are
already correct in the HTML; the same scripts run; `fetchCardSetsByYear`
loads the year and opens the set whose `setID` matches; `fetchPageTitle`
sets the same title and tags again plus breadcrumbs and the Product
structured data; on `window.load` the nav, footer, picker and masthead
render and the links are upgraded (below).

## Links: query hrefs, upgraded from the manifest

The nav, footer, breadcrumb category link, year picker and Player Search
results know a year or a `setID`, not a slug. They render with the
query-string `href` plus `data-review-cat` / `data-review-year` (or
`data-review-setid`) attributes. `helper.js` starts loading
`/reviews/index.json` as soon as it runs, and `applyReviewLinks()`
swaps in `/reviews/<slug>/` for every such link once it arrives.

The manifest is written by the same build as the pages, so it only ever
lists pages that exist in that deployment: no window where a link
points at a page that has not been built yet, no per-page API call, and
no way to drift from the pages. If it has not loaded, or a set is not in
it, the query link stays and still works (the page then rewrites its own
address). The CMS pages never load it.

A year's default set (the one a bare-year link opens) is the highest
rated, ties broken by set name A to Z. `compareSetsForDefault()` in
`helper.js` is that rule, and `wax.js` sorts a year's sets with the same
function, so the year links and the old bare-year URLs agree. (Before
2026-10-30 ties followed DynamoDB's order, which is arbitrary.)

## URL design

- **Slug.** The existing `seoURLSlug` field, now required in the CMS.
  Generate builds it from the set name; the client check
  (`seoSlugProblem()` in `cmsFormUI.js`), `createCardPost` and
  `updateCardSet` all enforce lowercase letters, numbers and single
  hyphens. Saving a live set also fails if another live set already uses
  the slug (a query of the `blogStatus-year-index` GSI), so the build's
  duplicate check can't be tripped from the CMS.
- **No `index.html` in the address.** Each page is written as
  `reviews/<slug>/index.html` and linked as `/reviews/<slug>/`. A web
  server answers a folder URL with that folder's `index.html`, the same
  way `/` shows the root `index.html`. A spike page confirmed it on
  Amplify: the slash form returns 200, the no-slash form 301s to it, and
  `/reviews/<slug>/index.html` also works. The folder layout was chosen
  over `<slug>.html` files because Amplify would only serve those at
  `/<slug>.html`, and a clean extensionless address would need one
  rewrite rule per set in the Amplify console (not in git). The canonical
  is the slash form, so the `/index.html` duplicate is harmless.
- **Old URLs.** `waxReviews.html?...` still works (above), including
  `&setID=` links. The 2004/mcd special case still redirects to the
  lockout page. A `sortOrder=last` parameter is dropped when the address
  is rewritten.
- **Social previews.** Facebook, Discord, Reddit and X read only the raw
  HTML, so only a slug URL gets a per-set preview; a shared old-style
  link gets the generic one.

## Where the pages physically live

Only inside the Amplify build artifact and the deployed site; not in git.
Amplify clones the repo onto a temporary build machine, the generator
writes `reviews/` and `sitemap.xml` into that checkout, Amplify zips
the whole directory and deploys it, and the machine is discarded.
`.gitignore` lists `/reviews/` and `/sitemap.xml`. To see them, fetch the
live URLs (for example `/reviews/index.json`); to get a local copy run
`node tools/generateReviewPages/generate.mjs`, which writes the same files
into the working folder (ignored by git). Because the artifact is the
whole repo, `amplify.yml` itself is also served at `/amplify.yml`, like
`tools/` and `Documentation/` already are.

## The rest of the build: minified assets

Since 2026-10-30 the same build also minifies the public scripts and the
stylesheet. It is described here because it shares `amplify.yml` and the
"generated in the build, never committed" rule with the review pages.

**What happens.** After the generator, `node tools/minifyAssets/minify.mjs`
rewrites the build's own copies of `scripts/helper.js`, `wax.js`,
`ticker.js`, `blogs.js`, `playerSearch.js`, `browseBySet.js`,
`timeline.js` and `styles/styles.css` in place, with a linked source map
(`helper.js.map` and so on, readable source embedded) beside each. The
URLs don't change and no HTML changes, so every page, including every
generated review page, picks the minified files up automatically. The repo
keeps readable source and nothing minified is committed; the build machine
is thrown away. The CMS scripts, `auth.js`, `scripts/fonts/*` (already
base64, nothing to gain), deprecated scripts and the inline `<script>`
blocks in the HTML are not touched.

**Why this way.** The site already served Brotli, so the gain is smaller
than raw sizes suggest but still about half: raw 260,043 to 135,417 bytes
across the 8 files, and over the wire about 67 KB to 34.5 KB (live:
`helper.js` 9.2 to 5.8 KB, `wax.js` 11.3 to 6.5 KB, `styles.css` 24.9 to
11.4 KB; a review page goes from about 56 KB to 28 KB, and the browser
parses less). Doing it in the build, not by committing minified copies,
means no drift between source and output, and the source stays what you
edit and read.

**The tool.** esbuild, installed by `npm ci` from a root `package.json`
and `package-lock.json` (the only dependency in the repo outside
`Lambdas/`), pinned to 0.19.12 because 0.19 is the last line that supports
the build image's Node 16. Each file is minified on its own, with no
bundling and no format option: esbuild then keeps every top-level
`function`, `let`, `const` and `var` name, which matters because inline
`onclick` handlers and calls between scripts rely on those names, and only
shortens local names. `rm -rf node_modules` runs last because the artifact
is the whole directory and would otherwise publish the installed packages;
that is also why `node_modules` isn't cached between builds (`npm ci` takes
about half a second here).

**Safety.** The tool overwrites files, so it refuses to run unless
`AWS_APP_ID` is set (Amplify sets it) or `--force-in-place` is passed;
`--root <dir>` points it at a scratch copy, which is how it was tested. It
fails the build, leaving the previous deployment live and the notifier
emailing the log, if any file is empty, not smaller, missing its source
map, or has lost a top-level name found at the start of a line in the
source (a regex check, so keep top-level declarations at the start of a
line). It must run after the generator, which reads the readable
`helper.js` and `waxReviews.html`.

**Working with it.** Edit the readable source only. A new public script or
stylesheet must be added to the list in `minify.mjs` or it ships unminified.
A production console error shows minified lines unless dev tools are open
(they fetch the `.map` and show the real file and line). The build log
prints the before and after bytes per file. `npm audit` prints a notice for
esbuild 0.19.12; it concerns esbuild's development server, which is never
run here, and moving to a newer esbuild needs a newer Node than the image
has.

**How it was verified.** On a scratch copy (generate, then minify): 46
browser checks gave identical results for the original and minified copies,
and 36 screenshots (12 pages at 1300, 768 and 390 px, with recorded API
data, a fixed random seed and fonts) were pixel-identical. On production
(build #3157): 10 pages at two widths with no console errors, links
upgraded, the checklist modal working, the `.map` files served and
`/node_modules/` returning 404.

## Why this is only a partial static site

The generated HTML contains the metadata but not the review. The review
text, the star and detail widgets, the checklist, the vote buttons and
the ticker are still fetched and drawn in the browser. That is enough for
what was needed: social crawlers only read the head, and Google runs
JavaScript and indexes the rendered body. It leaves two gaps: crawlers
that do not run JavaScript see no review text, and a visitor waits for
the API call before the review appears (the earlier "Houston" capture in
Search Console was a symptom of that dependence).

### Compared with an enterprise headless-CMS static setup

A typical enterprise setup (a headless CMS such as Contentstack feeding a
Next.js, Astro or Gatsby build) has the same shape: the CMS is the source
of truth, a publish event triggers a build, the build pulls content from a
delivery API, and static output goes to a CDN.

| Enterprise setup | This site |
|---|---|
| CMS with content types, fields and workflow | cardStack CMS plus the DynamoDB `Cards` table |
| Delivery API (token-protected, CDN-cached) | `getPublicCardSets` (public, cache header) |
| Publish webhook | DynamoDB Stream plus `cardsRebuildTrigger` |
| Framework build (Next, Astro, Gatsby) | `generate.mjs`, string replacement into one HTML file |
| Launch, Vercel or Netlify hosting | Amplify Hosting |
| Build alerts | `amplifyBuildNotifier` |

Where the enterprise version goes further:

- **Full prerendering.** The whole page, content included, is built
  ahead of time and the browser only adds interactivity. Here only the
  head is.
- **Incremental builds.** On-demand revalidation rebuilds just the changed
  page in seconds. Here every build regenerates all of the roughly 63
  pages and takes about two and a half minutes, which is fine at this size
  but would not scale to thousands of pages.
- **Content workflow.** Versioning and rollback, scheduled publishing,
  roles, audit logs, references between entries and localisation. Here a
  set is live or staged, with no history.
- **Preview.** Live preview against a draft API and a preview deployment
  per branch. Here the CMS preview modal, which shares
  `buildCardSetMarkup()` with the live page, and no staging site.
- **Templating.** Components, typed routing, image optimisation. Here one
  HTML file with marker comments that the generator checks for.

**Path to a full static setup.** The review markup comes from one shared
function, `buildCardSetMarkup()` in `helper.js`. The generator could run
it at build time with each set's full text and write the review into the
page, leaving the browser JavaScript to handle only votes, the checklist
modal and the ticker. That removes the API wait and gives non-JavaScript
crawlers the text. It needs a build-time source for the full review text
(the public list does not carry it) and that function running cleanly in
Node. Not planned.

## Failure modes and safeguards

- **Generator fails** (bad data, API down during the build, template
  markers broken): build fails, previous deployment stays live, the
  notifier emails the log link. While the API is down, builds started by
  unrelated pushes fail the same way.
- **Minifier fails** (a file not smaller, a missing source map or a lost
  top-level name, or `npm ci` unable to reach the npm registry): the build
  fails the same way, the previous deployment stays live and the notifier
  emails the log. A CMS save starts a build, so until it is fixed new
  content doesn't reach the site either.
- **Duplicate or invalid slug:** rejected at save time by the CMS Lambdas,
  so the generator's own check should never trip.
- **Build in progress or failed:** a freshly saved set's page does not
  exist for about three minutes. The links come from the manifest, so no
  link points at it before it exists. The admin page's **Review Pages
  Check** (`cms/admin.html`) requests every live set's page and lists any
  that are missing; a miss that persists means a failed build.
- **Stale static head** (a title or description changed but the build has
  not finished, or failed): affects only the raw-HTML social preview.
  The page's JavaScript corrects the tags for browsers and Google.
- **Trigger not firing:** check `/aws/lambda/cardsRebuildTrigger` in
  CloudWatch, and `aws amplify list-jobs --app-id d20qsyoicusf3p
  --branch-name main --region us-east-2` for a recent job.

## One-time AWS setup (done 2026-10-30)

1. DynamoDB, table `Cards`, Exports and streams: turn on the stream with
   **New and old images**.
2. Lambda `cardsRebuildTrigger` (Node, source in
   `Lambdas/cardsRebuildTrigger/index.mjs`, pasted into the console). Role
   permissions: the managed policy `AWSLambdaDynamoDBExecutionRole`, plus
   an inline policy allowing `amplify:StartJob` on
   `arn:aws:amplify:us-east-2:339740904141:apps/d20qsyoicusf3p/branches/main/jobs/*`.
3. Trigger on that Lambda: the `Cards` stream, batch size 100, batch
   window 60 seconds, starting position Latest, retry attempts 3.
4. The roles of `createCardPost` and `updateCardSet` each need an inline
   policy allowing `dynamodb:Query` on
   `arn:aws:dynamodb:us-east-2:339740904141:table/Cards/index/blogStatus-year-index`
   (for the duplicate-slug check; without it every live save fails).
5. `getPublicCardSets` must be the version that returns `stars`.

## Cost

Only Amplify build minutes. A build takes about 2.4 minutes (recent jobs
142 to 193 seconds) and is billed per build minute (about $0.01 at the
time of writing; check current pricing), so roughly $0.02 to $0.03 a
build, under $1 a month at around 30 saves, and inside the 1,000 free
build minutes a month while the account is within its free tier.
Reading a DynamoDB Stream from Lambda is free, the trigger Lambda and the
duplicate-slug query are negligible, and hosting grows by about 63 small
files. There are no standing charges. The manifest also removed the
per-page-view API call an earlier design needed. Installing esbuild and
minifying add about a second to a build (the log showed `npm ci` at 0.4 s
and the minifier at 0.1 s), so the build minutes don't change.

## Change log

- **2026-10-30 (later)** — Public JS and CSS minified in the build.
  - New `tools/minifyAssets/minify.mjs` (esbuild 0.19.12), run by
    `amplify.yml` after the generator; root `package.json` and
    `package-lock.json` added; `npm ci` before and `rm -rf node_modules`
    after, so the installed packages aren't published.
  - 7 public scripts and `styles/styles.css` minified in place with linked
    source maps: raw 260,043 to 135,417 bytes, about 67 KB to 34.5 KB over
    the wire. Verified on a scratch copy (46 checks, 36 pixel-identical
    screenshots) and on production (build #3157).
  - The cache for `node_modules` in the original plan was dropped: the
    artifact is the whole directory, so the folder is deleted instead.
- **2026-10-30** — Review pages moved from one query-string URL to
  generated `/reviews/<slug>/` pages.
  - SEO Friendly URL made required and validated (client, create and
    update Lambdas), with a duplicate check against live sets.
  - `tools/generateReviewPages` replaced `tools/generateSitemap`: it
    writes the pages, the manifest and the sitemap, and runs on every
    Amplify build (`amplify.yml`), so nothing is committed or run by
    hand. The year ranges it needed are now read from
    `scripts/helper.js` instead of being duplicated.
  - `waxReviews.html` became the generator's template (marker comments,
    global `setID`, absolute links) while still serving old URLs.
  - A save to a live set starts a build: Cards stream,
    `cardsRebuildTrigger`, `amplify:StartJob`.
  - Nav, footer, breadcrumb, year-picker and Player Search links switched
    to slug URLs via the build manifest; a year's default set is now
    highest stars, then name.
  - `getPublicCardSets` gained `stars` and the SEO and image fields.
  - Admin page gained the Review Pages Check.
  - The generated SEO title lost its " | Junk Wax Hockey" suffix.
  - Dead ends on the way, kept for context: links first built from the
    live API (they would have pointed at pages not yet built, and cost an
    API call per page view), a `?view=links` variant of
    `getPublicCardSets` for that (reverted), and a hand-run generator
    with the output committed (replaced by the build).
